brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Full bases stacked at cell (0,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0, piece:0,0,1, piece:0,0,2), with a half base on each side of the bottom storey; check_build reports meshClash clear and no issues.
Two drawers on level 0: drawer:0#-1,0#cut on half-n base (-1,0,0) and drawer:0#0,-1#cut on half-s base (0,-1,0).

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: Full-depth open bin bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full on the top-storey base (0,0,2), uncovered at the top.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey tower: a stacked column of hex bases at (0,0) with two drawers on the bottom storey and an open full-depth bin on the top storey. Open faces were capped and joints locked; check_build is clean (meshClash clear). The top storey has only one bin, since the brief did not specify a count. I did not add props.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
